### workspace run --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace run [project] <command> [options]

Send a shell command to a pane in a running project's tmux session.
Defaults to the bottommost pane. Auto-detects project from cwd if omitted.

Options:
        --pane N                     Target pane: zero-based index, 'window.pane' (e.g. '0.1', as shown by 'workspace sessions'), a tmux pane id (e.g. '%19', from 'workspace sessions --json'), 'bottom', or a title substring (e.g. 'Claude Code'). A title is matched against the raw pane title, then the agent label shown in 'workspace sessions' TITLE; the first matching pane wins, so use 'window.pane' or a '%id' to be exact
        --bottom                     Target the bottommost pane (default behavior)
        --split                      Create a new pane below the bottommost and run command there
        --vertical                   With --split, split side-by-side (vertical divider) instead of horizontal
        --no-enter                   Send command text without pressing Enter
        --focus                      Bring the project's iTerm window to the front after sending
        --dry-run                    Print the tmux command without executing it
        --wait                       Wait for the command to finish and report exit status, stdout, stderr
        --timeout N                  Seconds to wait (default: 300, requires --wait)
        --close                      Send 'exit' to the pane after the command runs (closes the shell/pane)
        --pipe CMD                   Pipe command output into CMD (repeatable for multi-stage pipelines)
        --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) naming the pane
                                     (the new pane's id with --split, else null); not with --wait or --dry-run

Exit codes: 0 delivered; 1 not delivered, safe to run again; 2 text
  landed but wasn't confirmed submitted — do not resend, check the pane first.

Examples:
  workspace run 'rake spec'    # bottommost pane, project auto-detected from cwd
  workspace run scooter 'rake spec' --pane 1    # explicit project and pane
  workspace run scooter 'bundle exec rails console' --no-enter    # pre-fill without pressing Enter
  workspace run scooter 'rake spec' --split    # run in a new pane below the bottommost
  workspace run scooter 'bin/dev' --split --vertical    # run in a new pane beside the bottommost
  workspace run scooter 'rake spec' --wait --timeout 60    # a script must block until the suite finishes, then act on its exit status (gives up after 60s)
  workspace run scooter 'rake spec' --split --wait --close    # run in a throwaway pane and close it when done
  workspace run scooter 'grep ERROR log/production.log' --pipe 'sort' --pipe 'uniq -c'    # count the distinct errors in a log, with each stage checked for quoting
  workspace run scooter 'rake spec' --dry-run    # check where the command would go before sending it
  workspace run scooter 'tail -f log/development.log' --split --json    # print an action document naming the new pane
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace run --bogus
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
invalid option: --bogus
--- end
### workspace run --bogus --json
--- exit 1
--- stdout
{"schema_version":1,"ok":false,"error":"invalid option: --bogus","code":"usage"}
--- stderr
--- end
### workspace run
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
Usage: workspace run [project] <command> [options]

Options:

        --bottom                     Target the bottommost pane (default behavior)
        --split                      Create a new pane below the bottommost and run command there
        --vertical                   With --split, split side-by-side (vertical divider) instead of horizontal
        --no-enter                   Send command text without pressing Enter

        --dry-run                    Print the tmux command without executing it
        --wait                       Wait for the command to finish and report exit status, stdout, stderr

        --pipe CMD                   Pipe command output into CMD (repeatable for multi-stage pipelines)
        --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) naming the pane
                                     (the new pane's id with --split, else null); not with --wait or --dry-run

Exit codes: 0 delivered; 1 not delivered, safe to run again; 2 text
